intent: Test whether forward look-ahead (sensors at y=0.07 m instead of 0.04 m) and a larger 16 mm footprint reduce line loss and max_error while keeping the iteration 1 drivetrain. The Integrator should check whether the controller can use the earlier signal without oscillating, and whether steering_oscillation rises. Compared with iteration 1, the single main change is the sensor geometry (forward offset and footprint).
learning: Hypotheses: (1) Forward sensors at y=0.07 m reduce max_error on s-bend and slalom versus iteration 1, because the controller sees bends earlier. (2) A 16 mm footprint lowers line_loss_events versus 12 mm at the same spread. (3) If max_error still sits at 0.06 m with few line losses, the limit is actuator lag, so the next step is lower mass or wheel_track changes, not more sensing. (4) If line losses stay high even with the 16 mm footprint, the next step is a wider spread (±0.05 m) with 7 sensors to keep the outer sensors on tape. Iteration 1 showed that spread alone does not help, so spread changes should be paired with a lookahead change.
rationale: Evidence: every development run in iterations 0 and 1 ended off track at max_error of about 0.06 m, the off-track limit. Line-loss events stayed at 1.0 to 1.35 per run. The wider ±0.036 m spread in iteration 1 did not reduce line losses (1.05 to 1.1 on s-bend and slalom, 1.05 on oval, against 1.35 on oval before). It also lowered oval progress from 0.72 to 0.62 and the score from 140 to 128. So sensor spread alone is not the binding limit. The off-track limit is max(0.06, 0.0125 + body_width/4), which stays at 0.06 m for any body width up to 0.18 m, so body width remains irrelevant. The likely limit is reaction lag: by the time the sensors register the line drifting, the wheels are already too far off. Two geometry levers address lag and blindness without changing the controller. (1) Move the sensors forward from y=0.04 to y=0.07 m, which puts them about 0.07 m ahead of the axle and gives more look-ahead on bends. The body front is at 0.08 m, so this stays inside the envelope. (2) Use the 16 mm footprint instead of 12 mm. At ±0.036 m spread, a 16 mm sensor keeps seeing tape to about 0.0565 m offset, against 0.054 m for 12 mm, and it gives smoother analogue readings that should cut dropouts. I keep the iteration 1 drivetrain (track 0.10 m, radius 0.035 m, mass 0.6 kg) so that the sensor change is the main variable being tested against iteration 1. Expected result: fewer line-loss events and a lower max_error on s-bend and slalom than iteration 1, with oval progress recovering toward 0.72 or better. Finishing on s-bend and slalom is still unlikely until the Integrator tunes the controller.
